root_idea.summary: The root centers on turning a thing upside down and returning its beginning to its end.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends from physical inversion to reversal, sending back, or returning from one state to another. The Quranic Form IV applies it to being cast back into unbelief or plunged into an adverse state; the related noun رِكْسٌ denotes rejected or filthy matter, explained as having been diverted from its original use.

senses.definition: To overturn, reverse, or cast someone back into an adverse or former state; in Quranic usage, to cast people back into unbelief or plunge them back into an evil condition.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively in the active; the Quranic passive occurrence expresses undergoing this reversal or being plunged back into the condition.

senses.definition: To separate or disperse people as a consequence of their disbelief and disobedience.
senses.usage_conditions: Recorded as an alternative interpretation of the Quranic use in the same construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn a thing over or upside down; to reverse its order or direction; figuratively, to overturn an enemy or change his state or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun رَكْسٌ denotes this act of turning over or reversal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To separate or set a thing apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct transitive use from physical reversal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn someone back or cause him to return to evil; also, to return a garment or piece of cloth to the dyeing liquor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional applications involving return to a prior or different condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become overturned, inverted, subverted, or reversed; to return or revert from one state to another; to fall back into a situation from which one had escaped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or reflexive Form VIII use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uncleanness, dirt, or filth; anything disliked because of its uncleanness, including excrement or rejected matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage, also treated as synonymous with رَجِيعٌ in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing turned over, upside down, or reversed; something turned or sent back or away; one who goes back or reverts from a state or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial and descriptive use covering reversed things and one who reverts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A weak person who returns or reverts from one thing or state to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet in the supplied Classical Arabic evidence.
